meta.game: Small Wants (formerly Greedy City) - 2D top-down pixel trading simulation
planner_assumptions: The four design files at repo root (GDD.md, game_model.json, sim.py, test_report.md, test_results.json) are LOCKED and read-only; every agent task treats them as reference inputs only.

test_report.md / test_results.json are the regression baseline; if a deliberate model change is ever approved, a dedicated re-tuning task regenerates goldens and updates the baseline in the same PR (never silently).
Each executing agent works one task per session with no shared memory; every task's context_pack is therefore self-sufficient and the repo itself (docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md) repeats the global conventions.
Godot 4.7.2-stable is fetched by CI and documented for local setup in docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md; agents do not need the Godot editor, only the CLI binary (producer directive 2026-11-26, D24).
One human (the studio owner) is available for: milestone playtests, art/music approval, publishing, and account management; all such tasks are marked human_required.
The 200-seed acceptance sweep takes about 64 seconds on the reference machine (measured, test_report.md), so nightly full sweeps are affordable in CI.
English is the only shipped language in 1.0; localization hooks land in M6 but no translation content is planned.
The on-device small model stays out of scope (GDD section 6: v1.1 post-launch); only its tags adapter interface is built (M3-T15).
Launch platforms are mobile-first: Android and iOS are the 1.0 ship targets; desktop (Win/Linux/macOS) presets keep building but the desktop release is post-1.0 (producer directive 2026-11-26, D14).

Data-driven mandate: no hardcoded data in Godot - every design number, roster, dialogue tag, palette band, audio rule and store copy loads from JSON at runtime; M7-T10's lint fails CI on content literals in .gd (D21).

The two producer-found simulation behaviors (threshold-vs-graph coarseness, single graph channel) are LOCKED-design facts: they are measured and documented (M7-T9, D22/D23), never silently redesigned; any retune is post-1.0 with owner sign-off.

tech_stack.choice: Godot 4.7.2-stable + GDScript; pure-logic GDScript layer (src/core, src/sim) with zero scene-tree dependencies, programmatic UI (no .tscn editing), custom canvas renderer; mobile-first export targets (Android + iOS); Python stays as the golden/reference toolchain (sim.py + tools/*).

alternatives_considered.pros: Mature headless test tooling (vitest), trivial CI, static-site shipping, node crypto gives sha512 for free.
alternatives_considered.cons: Ships a browser build while the producer directive (2026-11-26) locks mobile-first (iOS/Android) shipping and defers desktop; no editor tooling; the repo's curated agent skill library targets Godot; engine features (audio buses, input maps, export) would be re-built by hand.

alternatives_considered.option: Python + Pygame (closest to sim.py, zero port)
alternatives_considered.pros: No parity port at all; agents know Python.
alternatives_considered.cons: No iOS/Android export path at all (mobile-first is the producer's platform decision), and desktop packaging (PyInstaller per-OS) is the least reliable ship path; 60fps tile rendering with 30 NPCs is workable but wasteful; no scene/audio/export tooling; UI code is the hardest to keep testable.
Binary meta/scene files are hostile to many small AI edits; licensing; heavier CI; not needed for 2D pixel scope.

tech_stack.why: Producer directives (2026-11-26) pin the engine at Godot 4.7.2 and the launch platforms at mobile-first (iOS & Android, desktop later), superseding GDD 1.3's PC-desktop lock - the contradiction is logged as D14, not redesigned. Godot exports Android (AAB/APK), iOS (IPA) and Win/Linux/macOS from one GDScript codebase, so the mobile-first decision costs no architectural change. Godot 4 GDScript uses float64, so the sim.py port can match Python float arithmetic bit-for-bit in practice (machine-anchored goldens cover any libm residue). Everything stays text files (.gd/.json) that AI agents edit well. Game logic runs headless via 'godot --headless --script', which satisfies the parity requirement without graphics. Decisive: the repo already ships a curated skills/ library for Godot (gdscript, headless testing, tilemap, 2d movement, audio, export, UI, shaders) - free context for every executing agent.
constraints: Pinned engine version Godot 4.7.2-stable (CI downloads the pinned binary and verifies its sha256; upgrades are an explicit task, never incidental).
src/core and src/sim must never reference scene-tree classes (Node, Control, ...); they are plain RefCounted classes testable with --headless. A static grep test enforces this.
No use of Godot's RNG (randi, randf, randomize) anywhere in src/core or src/sim; parity requires the ported Python RNG (pyrng.gd). A grep test enforces this.

UI is built programmatically in GDScript (Control nodes in _ready); the only scene file is game/main.tscn. Agents never hand-edit .tscn resources, which removes merge-conflict and hallucinated-scene risk.

game_model.json is loaded at runtime by game/src/core/model.gd and checksummed; nothing in src/ hardcodes a design number. Data-driven mandate (producer directive, D21): ALL content - rosters, dialogue tags, palette bands, audio rules, schedules, store copy - loads from JSON data files; tools/check_data_driven.py (M7-T10) fails CI on content literals in .gd outside the engine-constants whitelist.
World/visual randomness uses a separate rng key namespace ('wx-...') so content noise can never perturb parity seeds.
Upgrades and other sim_coverage 'abstracted' features are implemented in the game but disabled in parity mode (--parity flag) so game-only systems cannot pollute the sim baseline.

Mobile-first: Android (AAB/APK, arm64-v8a + armeabi-v7a) and iOS (IPA) are the 1.0 ship targets with touch-first input; desktop presets (Win/Linux/macOS) are built and smoke-tested in CI but their release is post-1.0 (D14); no web export in 1.0.

principles: Vertical slices: every milestone ends with a build a human can launch and play, even if ugly.
Numbers come from game_model.json at runtime, never from an agent's memory or from GDD tables; sim.py is the executable reference.
Logic never touches nodes; rendering never computes rules. If a UI file needs a rule, it asks the logic layer.
Tests first: no task lands without its spec file and a green headless run. 'Looks good' is not a test; where feel is judged, the task says human_required with a checklist.

Parity is sacred: pinned-seed runs of the ported logic must match sim.py goldens (discrete fields exact, floats within 1e-6 relative). If parity breaks, the port is wrong - never 'fix' a golden to make a test pass.
One file, one owner: outputs list files a task creates; later tasks that modify them list them in inputs. This is enforced by validate_plan.py.
Small tasks only: one agent, one session, <=5 files, tests that finish in <5 minutes. Split anything bigger.
Determinism everywhere: same seed, same bytes - runs, goldens, snapshots, and bot traces.
Placeholder-first: no human asset blocks a build; placeholders are generated by tools/placeholder_*.py and swappable at paths recorded in docs/asset_manifest.md.
Licensing is not optional: every asset ships with provenance in docs/asset_manifest.md before M8.
Design contradictions are logged, not silently resolved: add a decisions_log entry citing GDD section and the resolution, and follow game_model.json's number.
Flaky tests get fixed or quarantined the same day (docs/QA_POLICY.md); a red CI is a stop-the-line event.
Data-driven or dead: if a value can change without recompiling logic, it lives in JSON. Any content literal in a .gd file is a bug and M7-T10's lint fails CI on it (D21).
Mobile is the platform (D14): every UI task sizes targets for fingers, not cursors, and keeps the mid-range Android device budget in mind; desktop is a post-1.0 convenience, not the default.

decisions_log.decision: Engine: Godot 4.7.2-stable + GDScript over TypeScript/Canvas and Python/Pygame (version pinned per producer directive, 2026-11-26; supersedes the 4.3 pin of plan v1.0.0 - see D24).
decisions_log.rationale: Producer pins 4.7.2; Godot exports iOS/Android/Win/Linux/macOS from one codebase, runs logic headless, uses float64 like Python, and the repo already ships a curated Godot skills/ library. The bump happens before execution starts, so no ported code exists to debug.

decisions_log.decision: Parity definition: pinned seeds, machine-anchored goldens; discrete fields exact, floats abs diff <= 1e-6 relative.
decisions_log.rationale: Bit-for-bit float equality across languages is not guaranteed through libm transcendental functions (rng.gauss); anchoring goldens to the CI image plus a 1e-6 tolerance gives a hard, testable contract.

decisions_log.decision: Pinned seed sets: per-PR runs seeds [1,2,3,42,777,1337,31337] x 6 bots + city gen 0..24 + m2 suite 24 seeds x 6 bots; nightly expands to 200 seeds/strategy.
decisions_log.rationale: test_report.md shows the 1,200-run sweep costs ~64s in Python; the game port is faster; 24x6 catches practically all regressions per PR while nightly keeps the full acceptance suite honest.

decisions_log.decision: Python RNG (MT19937 + str-seed sha512 + gauss cache) is re-implemented as pyrng.gd; Godot's RNG is banned in src/core and src/sim (grep-enforced).
decisions_log.rationale: sim.py's determinism contract (game_model.json -> meta.determinism) is defined by CPython's random module including string seeds like 'city-0'; there is no shortcut.

decisions_log.decision: UI is programmatic GDScript; the only scene file is game/main.tscn; tiles render through a custom draw-based node instead of TileMap.
decisions_log.rationale: Removes .tscn merge conflicts and the riskiest Godot APIs from agent hands; keeps everything text and greppable; a draw-based renderer is trivially deterministic.

decisions_log.decision: File ownership convention: outputs = files the task creates/owns; later tasks modifying them list the file in inputs; validate_plan.py enforces output uniqueness.
decisions_log.rationale: Gives every file exactly one creator so parallel agents never write the same file blind.

decisions_log.decision: game_model.json is read at runtime and checksummed; no design number is hardcoded in src/.
decisions_log.rationale: Keeps JSON the single source of truth and makes any number change a visible, testable event (R7).

decisions_log.decision: Upgrades (and other sim.py-abstracted features per game_model.json -> sim_coverage) are implemented in the game but disabled in parity mode via a --parity flag.
decisions_log.rationale: sim_coverage explicitly keeps them out of the loop math; the flag lets the game replay sim goldens without game-only coin effects.

decisions_log.decision: World/visual randomness uses a separate 'wx-' key namespace, never the parity seeds.
decisions_log.rationale: Content noise (tile scatter, schedule jitter) must not perturb the simulated economy or parity.

decisions_log.decision: 1.0 ships English-only with localization hooks (string tables + extraction tool) in M6; translations post-launch.
decisions_log.rationale: GDD does not require launch translations; hooks keep the cost of adding them later low.

decisions_log.decision: On-device small model is out of scope for 1.0; M3-T15 builds only the tags adapter interface (text->tags, tags->voice, menu fallback) per GDD section 6.
decisions_log.rationale: GDD locks the model for v1.1 post-launch; the interface-only hook is the agreed preparation.

decisions_log.decision: Telemetry is local-only (append-only JSON log + explicit export button); no network calls in the shipped game.
decisions_log.rationale: Cheap, privacy-safe balance data for the human team; matches the offline-friendly pixel game; grep test forbids HTTPRequest in src/.

decisions_log.decision: Danger meter is never rendered as a number (warning banners only) - enforced by a UI spec assertion.
decisions_log.rationale: GDD 1.4 and 5.3 lock this; a test prevents a well-meaning agent from 'improving' the HUD.

decisions_log.decision: Launch platforms are mobile-first: Android and iOS are the 1.0 ship targets; desktop (Win/Linux/macOS) presets are maintained and smoke-tested in CI but the desktop release is post-1.0. No web/itch-browser export in 1.0.
decisions_log.rationale: Producer directive (2026-11-26) supersedes GDD section 1.3's PC-desktop lock; per planning rule 11 the contradiction is logged here, not redesigned - the GDD platform section is treated as 'desktop later'. Mobile export presets and the store pipeline land in M8; touch input was already the plan's primary input model (tap/click, M1-T6), so no earlier milestone churns.

decisions_log.decision: All tasks are size S or M; nothing is size L.
decisions_log.rationale: Planning rule 4: anything bigger would exceed one agent session; the plan splits the sim port into 14 pass-level tasks instead of one 'port the economy' task.

decisions_log.decision: Deliberate deviations already in the design (fair deals greed-neutral, peak-greed latch, pressure-conditional relapse) are ported as-is, with test_report.md as the arbiter.
decisions_log.rationale: GDD section 8 documents them as measured decisions; agents must not 'fix' them.

decisions_log.decision: The morning report is generated from night diffs by the same ported code that sim.py uses (morning_report, sim.py lines 602-616), and its exact text is part of parity.
decisions_log.rationale: Text equality is the cheapest strong check that UI-facing state matches the reference; sample outputs exist in test_report.md.

decisions_log.decision: NPCs do not collide with the player or each other (walk-through); collision exists only against walls/water. NPC schedules are presentation-only.
decisions_log.rationale: GDD does not specify NPC-player collision; walk-through avoids path-blocking softlocks and keeps schedules deterministic. Logged as a resolved design gap.

decisions_log.decision: Shop upgrades are game-only depth (sim.py abstracts them per sim_coverage); exact in-game semantics: shelf = +1 trade slot per day; sign = fair-deal witness ripple x1.5; back_room = Break-in events take coins but never touch stored goods or learned secrets; teapot = a 5th action every other day. All disabled in parity mode (D8) and unit-pinned in spec_shop.
decisions_log.rationale: The model gives effect strings but no sim-side mechanics (abstracted); the game must fix precise rules or agents will invent inconsistent ones. Resolutions reuse existing resolver/event code paths only.

decisions_log.decision: Goldens are committed to the repo under game/tests/golden/ and regenerated only by tools/gen_golden.py in the same PR as any model change.
decisions_log.rationale: Keeps regression targets reviewable in diffs; prevents hand-edited goldens.

decisions_log.decision: Data-driven architecture mandate (producer directive): no hardcoded data in Godot - every design number, roster, dialogue tag, palette band, audio rule, schedule and store copy loads from JSON (game_model.json + generated data packs) at runtime.
decisions_log.rationale: Extends D7 from 'no design numbers in src/' to all content. Enforcement: M0-T4 schema assertions + checksum, and M7-T10's tools/check_data_driven.py --strict lint (fails CI on content literals in .gd outside the engine-constants whitelist). Benefit: balance/content edits never touch code, and AI agents cannot invent numbers.

decisions_log.decision: Producer-found weakness 1 (graph too small for thresholds to matter): verified against the locked design - across 200 generated cities (6,000 people) 66.2% have exactly 2 neighbors (degree histogram 2:3975, 3:1705, 4:284, 5:33, 6:3; ring within district + 6 cross-district pairs, sim.py lines 122-134), so greedy_frac takes values {0, 0.5, 1.0}; pride (0.50) and envy (0.35) tip on identical fractions for degree-2 people with ordinary (weight-1) neighbors; fear (0.60) requires both neighbors greedy. 'Envy tips first' (the 0.35 <= frac < 0.50 band) can only occur with hub weights (2.0) or degree >= 4, i.e. around hubs or extra ties. Design is LOCKED: no threshold or graph redesign.
decisions_log.rationale: Plan response: (a) behavior is pinned by the existing parity goldens (M2-T12) so any accidental change is caught; (b) M7-T9 adds tools/topology_report.py emitting the degree histogram and per-threshold tip rates per degree class, and docs/sim_behavior_notes.md records the numbers in-repo; (c) any retune (raise mean degree, split pride/envy thresholds) is post-1.0 and requires owner sign-off + golden regeneration (open assumptions).

decisions_log.decision: Producer-found weakness 2 (only one channel uses the graph): verified in sim.py - gossip_pass picks seeded random targets with a 70% same-district bias (sim.py line ~415) and never reads neighbor lists; market prices act on Market Square or all districts (game_model.json -> market.price_reasons); only contagion_pass iterates neighbor lists. The social graph carries exactly one of the three channels.
decisions_log.rationale: Design locked; the three-channel structure matches the GDD, so this is a fidelity note, not a bug. Response: M7-T9's topology report quantifies each channel's spread vs graph topology (% of gossip targets that are neighbors; price reasons reaching non-adjacent districts); gossip-along-edges and price-locality are logged as post-1.0 design-change requests needing owner approval.

decisions_log.decision: Engine pin bumped Godot 4.3-stable -> 4.7.2-stable in plan v1.1.0, BEFORE execution starts (cheap now, expensive later).
decisions_log.rationale: Parity is machine-anchored (gaps_report W1): vectors and goldens must be generated ON the 4.7.2 toolchain. M0-T2 pins the CI binary URL+sha256 for 4.7.2; M0-T3/M0-T6 regenerate the RNG known-answer vectors and city goldens against the pinned binary in the same tasks; if a 4.7.2 libm/VM difference shifts floats, it is caught at M0 with zero ported code to debug.

open_assumptions: A human artist/musician will be available by M5 for final art and chiptune approval; until then placeholder generation covers all art/audio tasks (R5).
Google Play developer account and Apple Developer Program membership exist by M8-T7 (signing keys are human-held); desktop store access (itch/Steam) is post-1.0 and not needed for the 1.0 ship gate.

Godot 4.7.2-stable remains the pinned version through the 1.0 ship (producer directive, D24); an engine upgrade mid-run is out of scope unless a blocking bug appears, and would re-trigger M0-T3/M0-T6 vector+golden regeneration.
The studio owner can do a ~30-60 minute human playtest at each milestone gate (9 gates).
sim.py stays frozen; if upstream design work resumes and changes it, the plan restarts at M0-T7 golden regeneration plus impact analysis of every parity task.
CI runners provide 2+ cores so the nightly 200-seed sweep stays inside 30 minutes.
The Grelwater canonical roster (game_model.json -> canonical_city) is exactly what sim.py --freeze-roster prints today; M0-T6 asserts it and would fail loudly on any mismatch.
English text needs no special font shaping; if a later locale requires complex shaping, the M6 i18n hook task gets a follow-up (out of scope).
A mid-range Android reference device (and, for iOS, one physical TestFlight device) is available to the human for the M8 device-smoke gate.
Post-1.0 design-change requests from D22 (threshold/degree retune) and D23 (gossip-along-edges, price-locality) await an explicit owner decision; the plan schedules no work for them.
